title: When the Prom Turns
premise: Lior Almeida, a senior debate champion, has spent years perfecting the art of not arguing with his mother about the family's fading orchard and his father's unexplained departure. When a college essay prompt — 'Describe a truth you were forced to inherit' — cracks him open, he discovers his late father's letters implicating the school board in burying a contaminated water report that sickened students a decade ago. As prom season becomes the board's celebratory cover story, Lior must choose between the safe future he's argued for and the truth that could cost him everything. He publishes the letters the night of prom, wins nothing gracefully, loses some things permanently, and finally understands that inheritance isn't what you're given — it's what you refuse to pass on.
about_author: Ansel Nystrom is a former high school debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers win arguments they couldn't have at home. They write in a converted cider barn in rural Oregon, where the apple trees are older than anyone willing to admit.

chapters.title: The Art of Conceding
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He wins the regional debate final on a technicality while mentally rehearsing the conversation he won't have with his mother about selling the orchard. At home, he concedes every point before she makes it. Emotional beat: the hollowness of winning everywhere except where it counts.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In college essay workshop, prompt four — 'a truth you were forced to inherit' — silences the room. Lior writes three false drafts, then one true sentence he immediately deletes: 'My father didn't leave because of us.' Emotional beat: the first crack in a carefully maintained story.

chapters.title: What the Attic Kept
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, shifting to brief flashbacks in his father's voice through letters. Hunting college materials, Lior finds a locked tin: unsent letters and a 2014 water quality report stamped WITHHELD by the district. His father was the facilities manager who tried to speak. Emotional beat: grief reorganizing itself into something sharper.

chapters.title: The Prom Committee Has Answers
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Lior and Priya Raghavan, student body president and his debate rival. The board announces a lavish 'legacy prom' funded by an anonymous donor — the same week Lior starts asking quiet questions. Priya notices him noticing. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between two people trained to detect lies.

chapters.title: Marisol Vega Was in That Classroom
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She reveals her older sister Marisol drank from the east-wing fountains during the contamination window and has been sick since. Her family took a settlement with a gag clause. Emotional beat: the abstract becomes a face at Lior's kitchen table, and his mother recognizes Marisol's mother — they were friends.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. His mother finds the letters and detonates: not with anger but terror, revealing she knew, that the settlement bought their silence too, that the orchard's failing well is the same aquifer. She demands he stop. For the first time, Lior doesn't concede. Emotional beat: the argument he's avoided for four years, finally had — and lost differently than expected.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Lior and Priya pitch the story to the school paper; the advisor kills it within hours, then the board offers Lior a 'leadership scholarship' with strings attached. His best friend Theo distances himself, scared of association. Emotional beat: isolation as pressure — money, silence, and loyalty all pulling the same direction.

chapters.title: The Rebuttal
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He does what he does best: builds the case. Letters, the withheld report, Marisol's medical records (with her consent), the donor traced to a board member's brother-in-law. Priya helps structure it like a debate brief. They plan to release everything during prom, when every family in town will be watching. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into preparation.

chapters.title: When the Prom Turns
chapters.summary: Dual POV, climax. Mid-prom, under the legacy banner, the documents hit every phone in the gym via QR code printed in the program. The board member confronts Lior publicly; instead of defending himself, Lior reads his father's final letter aloud over the sound system. Half the room walks out; half stays to dance. Emotional beat: truth as both rupture and strange celebration.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue weeks later. State investigation opened; the board resigns; the scholarship offer rescinded, replaced by something smaller and honest. His mother plants new trees on the orchard's edge — over clean soil, after remediation. Lior submits the essay, all of it, unedited. Final beat: he keeps his father's last letter, and answers it.
